bridge

Reusable native integrations for web applications.

Bridge connects web applications to native platform capabilities. Small, stable, well-documented interfaces that hide platform-specific complexity.

GitHub Documentation

The problem

Web applications need native capabilities: secure storage, biometrics, file access, share sheets, offline downloads. Each platform implements these differently. Without a shared layer, every application rebuilds the same bridges.

The approach

Bridge provides a single interface for native capabilities. One TypeScript API, implemented in Kotlin for Android and Swift for iOS. Applications call the web interface. Bridge handles the platform-specific work.

No unnecessary abstraction. No generic frameworks. Just small, focused plugins that solve real problems shared by multiple projects.

Principles

  • Quiet. The interface should almost disappear.
  • Stable. API compatibility maintained across versions.
  • Documented. Every plugin includes examples and platform notes.
  • Tested. TypeScript, Android, and iOS tests for every plugin.
  • Shared. Added only when at least two projects need it.

Current state

Bridge is a foundation. No plugins are implemented yet. The first plugin will be added when a second project needs the same native capability.

This is intentional. Premature abstraction adds maintenance without adding value. Real need drives real design.

Structure

  • packages/bridge-core/ — core utilities
  • packages/example-app/ — development playground
  • docs/ — design language and philosophy
